routes.label: Use divisibility by11 for a lower bound and exhibit a valid sum

question: A palindrome is a number that has the same value when read from left to right or from right to left. (For example, \(12321\) is a palindrome.) Let \(N\) be the least three-digit integer which is not a palindrome but which is the sum of three distinct two-digit palindromes. What is the sum of the digits of \(N?\)
solution:
Every two-digit palindrome has the same two digits, so it is one of \(11,22,\ldots,99\). These are all multiples of \(11\), which means any sum of three of them is also a multiple of \(11\).

The least three-digit multiple of \(11\) is \(110\). It meets the remaining conditions: it is not a palindrome, and

\[
110=22+33+55
\]

uses three distinct two-digit palindromes. Thus \(N=110\), whose digit sum is \(1+1+0=\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

The divisibility observation gives a lower bound, and the displayed sum shows that bound is attainable.
